question_en: What are the manufacturer and specific model of the accessory shown in the image?
gold_trajectory:
# Detailed Simulated Search Trajectory · 2-2-F02

## Step 01 · Extract structural clues from the microhardness accessory

**Action:** Record the long gray sliding stage, the separated positions of the objective and indenter, the paired front clamps, and the central adjustment component. Use "microscope microhardness tester sliding attachment separate objective indenter" as search terms, then compare with similar equipment from Zeiss Jena.

**Evidence Observation:** The current displayed orientation differs from the direction when mounted on a microscope; the right-side indenter is exposed, and an empty threaded mounting position is visible in the center. First, look for similar devices based on the long sliding stage shared by two working positions, rather than naming it only by the broad category of microscope accessories.

## Step 02 · Correlate with original product photos and multiple views of the same item

**Action:** Consult the microscopeparts entry 99042 and its image gallery to verify photo 154236_909 corresponding to the question image; use adjacent angles to confirm the sliding stage and clamps, rather than treating each angle as an independent specimen.

Source entry, image gallery, and target original image:
https://www.microscopeparts.eu/part/carl-zeiss-jena-vertival-microscope-mhp-160-microhardness-tester-99042

https://www.microscopeparts.eu/gallery/99042-carl-zeiss-jena-vertival-microscope-mhp-160-microhardness-tester

https://www.mikroskopteile.eu/foto/owner-1/99042-Carl-Zeiss-Jena-Vertival-microscope-hardness-tester/Carl-Zeiss-Jena_microscope-MHP-160-microhardness-tester_IMG_20260217_154236_909.jpg

Other views of the same equipment:
https://www.mikroskopteile.eu/foto/owner-1/99042-Carl-Zeiss-Jena-Vertival-microscope-hardness-tester/Carl-Zeiss-Jena_microscope-MHP-160-microhardness-tester_IMG_20260217_154246_303.jpg

https://www.mikroskopteile.eu/foto/owner-1/99042-Carl-Zeiss-Jena-Vertival-microscope-hardness-tester/Carl-Zeiss-Jena_microscope-MHP-160-microhardness-tester_IMG_20260217_154253_900.jpg

https://www.mikroskopteile.eu/foto/owner-1/99042-Carl-Zeiss-Jena-Vertival-microscope-hardness-tester/Carl-Zeiss-Jena_microscope-MHP-160-microhardness-tester_IMG_20260217_154304_696.jpg

https://www.mikroskopteile.eu/foto/owner-1/99042-Carl-Zeiss-Jena-Vertival-microscope-hardness-tester/Carl-Zeiss-Jena_microscope-MHP-160-microhardness-tester_IMG_20260217_154307_161.jpg

https://www.mikroskopteile.eu/foto/owner-1/99042-Carl-Zeiss-Jena-Vertival-microscope-hardness-tester/Carl-Zeiss-Jena_microscope-MHP-160-microhardness-tester_IMG_20260217_154312_755.jpg

**Evidence Observation:** The outline of the long sliding stage, the open indenter, the empty objective position, and the front clamps correspond; the entry provides MHP-160 as a candidate. "Vertival" in the title refers to the compatible microscope name and cannot replace the accessory's own model number. The seller's name alone is insufficient to prove the model; continue verifying against the manual structure.

## Step 03 · Verify model and differences with neighboring models using the original manufacturer's manual

**Action:** Read mhp 160 manual §2.1 and Figures 1, 4, 5 to compare the relationship between the indenter, objective, and shared sliding stage; simultaneously check the same manufacturer's D32 and mhp 100.

mhp 160 original manufacturer manual:
https://www.mikroskopteile.eu/foto/owner-1/_manuals/Carl-Zeiss-Jena-MHP-160.pdf

**Evidence Observation:** In the mhp 160, the objective and indenter are installed at different positions on the same movable sliding stage, matching the two-workstation structure in the question image. Figures 1, 4, and 5 in the D32 manual show a more compact enclosed cylindrical assembly, lacking the long dual-workstation layout seen in the question image. The text description for mhp 100 places the indenter in front of the objective; the preserved 20-page text version lacks complete plates, so screw positions are not fabricated based on it.

D32 manual (relevant figures on PDF pages 9, 11, 12) and mhp 100 text:
https://www.mikroskop-online.de/mikroskope/wp-content/uploads/simple-file-list/Zeiss-Jena-Bedienanleitungen-Druckschriften-mikroskopischen-Zusatz-Ergaenzungsgeraeten/30-676c-1_G-Mikrohaerterpruefeinrichtung-D32-TB.pdf

https://www.mikroskop-online.de/Mikroskop%20BDA/30-676e-1.G%20%20Mikrohaertepruefeinrichtung%20mhp%20100%20%28T%29.pdf

Historical catalog index and small accompanying images for mhp 100, useful for viewing the overall structure but not for distinguishing small parts:
https://antiquemicroscopes.co.uk/imagedatabasecataloguesgermanyzeiss.html

https://antiquemicroscopes.co.uk/imagedatabasecataloguesgermanyzeiss.fld/image663.png

The Leitz MINILOAD with similar function features a rotating head configuration, which differs significantly from the linear sliding stage here; it serves only as an external reference:
https://www.microscopemuseum.eu/catalogues/Ernst_Leitz_1966_Miniload_hardness_tester.pdf

## Step 04 · Finalize manufacturer and model, conclude identification

**Action:** Combine the original photo match with the structural description of mhp 160, using manufacturer VEB Carl Zeiss Jena and model mhp 160.

Manual archive entry available for re-checking the original text:
https://www.mikroskop-online.de/mikroskope/anleitungen/?ee=1&eeFolder=Zeiss-Jena-Bedienanleitungen-Druckschriften-mikroskopischen-Zusatz-Ergaenzungsgeraeten&eeListID=1

**Evidence Boundary:** The photos and manual support the device identity but do not support the calibration status, manufacturing year, or the seller's factory source of this equipment. Scale numbers are also not model numbers.

**Stopping Condition:** Both requested fields are supported by specific photos and structural documents; do not continue searching for the host microscope or measurement performance.

## Formal Answer

VEB Carl Zeiss Jena；mhp 160
